title: Co-PiLOT: Constrained Physics-Informed Latent Optimization for Target-Driven Inverse Design
claim: A generic optimization loop of generative decoder, physics simulator and active-learning optimizer is instantiated concretely for a specific scientific design domain.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right flow, dashed zoom lines linking general to specific
description: Two stacked rounded panels linked by dashed zoom lines. The top panel is the general Co-PiLOT framework. A latent vector z, drawn as a blue box with a box constraint and a pool of encodings, feeds a green pre-trained decoder. The output goes through a yellow chevron domain bridge, then a physics oracle (orange header), then a purple scalar objective J. A dashed-line active-learning loop sits underneath. It holds a surrogate model, an acquisition function, a candidate batch and an observation history, and it returns a new z. The bottom panel repeats the same layout for magnesium-alloy microstructure. It adds a diffusion-transformer decoder, an RGB microstructure image, an orientation codec, a voxel grid, a crystal plasticity stress-strain plot, and the MERIDIAN optimizer. The optimizer contains a deep-kernel GP, an acquisition function, a DPP batch, a feasibility classifier and a trust region. Colors encode module types.
caption: CO-PILOT. (a) General framework and its materials instantiation (b): a Mg-alloy latent z⋆∈Z is passed through a decoder D like DIT or FM-DIT, bridged via an orientation codec (Ψ) to a .dream3d grid, scored by a crystal plasticity oracle f, and reduced to a fitness J (JV 1/JV 2) that the MERIDIAN optimizer O feeds back as znew for the next iteration. Physics enters via the simulator-based objective and feasibility model, and via codec-encoded training data (Sec. 3).
abstract: Inverse design of physical systems (molecules, devices, microstructures) often reduces to optimizing a high-dimensional structure against an expensive black-box simulator. Direct search is difficult because the space is non-Euclidean, feasibility is hard to encode, and each evaluation is expensive. We present Co-PiLOT, a latent optimization approach that maps candidates through a generative encoder-decoder, uses the decoder as a learned validity prior, and searches the latent space with physics-informed black-box optimization. The framework is applied on the inverse design of magnesium alloy microstructure/texture. We develop a vision transformer based-encoder; paired with latent diffusion, diffusion transformer and rectified-flow transformer-based decoders on $\sim80{,}000$ EBSD-derived microstructure dataset to learn a minimal bottleneck, $z$. The ViT-FMDiT model ($z$=$768$) reconstructs high-fidelity microstructure images (FID $27.86$, MS-SSIM $0.178$), which our self-segmenting orientation codec converts into input grids for crystal plasticity solver. Finally, we introduce MERIDIAN, an active latent optimizer driven by deep-kernel Gaussian-process uncertainty, failure-aware feasibility prediction, manifold-aware trust regions, and target-aware acquisition. Within a budget of $160$ simulations, the ViT-FMDiT and MERIDIAN combination yields the best target-driven objective score, reducing the relative target error by $3$--$22\%$ against seven baselines (DANTE, TuRBO, BAxUS, CMA-ES, DDOM, SEIKO, DDPO) on the same decoder.
